chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Ja’far narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Abī ‘Uthmān, from Ismā’īl ibn ‘Abbād, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali, from Abī Sa’īd Al-Madā’ini, who said:

I entered upon Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, should I go to the grave of Ḥusain?' He said, 'Yes, O Abā Sa’īd! Go to the grave of the son of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family), the most blessed of the blessed ones, the most purified of the purified ones, and the most pious of the pious ones; for if you visit him, twenty-two ‘Umrah will be registered for you.'

key_terms.أَبَرِّ الْأَبْرَارِ: The most pious of the pious ones
key_terms.أَطْهَرِ الطَّاهِرِينَ: The most purified of the purified ones
key_terms.أَطْيَبِ الطَّيِّبِينَ: The most blessed of the blessed ones
key_terms.ابْنُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Son of the Messenger of God
key_terms.قَبْرُ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Husain (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husain (a.s.) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elevates the visitation of Imam al-Husain (a.s.) by attributing to him the superlative titles of the most fragrant, pure, and righteous, thereby linking his physical presence to spiritual purity. The specific reward of twenty-two 'Umrah pilgrimages underscores the unique status of Karbala as a focal point of devotion in Shia tradition, where the sacrifice of the Imam is viewed as a means of attaining nearness to God comparable to the repeated pilgrimage to the Kaaba.
